briefing/resident:A01:
You are A01. You play a match of chess games against A02; the colours swap from game to game. A win counts 1 point, a draw half a point. Each game starts from a fresh mind.

When it is your move you are shown the position: play one legal move with playMove and end your turn. viewBoard shows the position again. An illegal move is refused and the board does not change; try another. Resign only in a lost position.

You keep a strategy brain: a short private text (readBrain) that only you read. Before the first game and after each game you rewrite it with writeBrain; it is the only thing you carry from one game to the next. Write the principles you want to play by, not a list of the moves.

chess/chess/advise: Your side ({{colour}}) is on move; {{captain}} plays it. Look at the position and advise {{captain}} in the team chat with postTeam: one short post with the move you suggest and why (a threat, a capture, a check). Then end your turn.
chess/chess/cap-settled: At the move cap a capture still open on the board counts: before the material is counted, the side to move is credited with the most it can win with one capture.
chess/chess/coach-clean: Coach: none of your {{total}} moves lost material or missed a free capture by a one-ply material check (it sees hanging pieces and free captures, not deeper tactics).
chess/chess/coach-review:
Coach: {{count}} of your {{total}} moves lost material or missed a free capture by a one-ply material check (it sees hanging pieces and free captures, not deeper tactics). The worst:
{{moves}}
chess/chess/forfeit-warning: You have not played a legal move for a while. After {{left}} more turn(s) without a move, a random legal move is played for you.
chess/chess/fresh-context: You start this half-move from a fresh mind: what you thought on earlier moves is gone. Below are the rules, your notes and the position. The reason you give with playMove is shown to you on your next move, so put your plan in it.
chess/chess/how-to-move: Play one move with playMove (for example Nf3, exd5, O-O, e8=Q, or g1f3); a short reason helps the record. Then end your turn.
chess/chess/last-note: Your note with your last move ({{moveNo}}. {{san}}): {{text}}
chess/chess/rules: Game {{game}} of {{games}}: you play {{colour}} against {{opponent}}. Standard chess rules (castling, en passant, promotion; checkmate wins; stalemate, threefold repetition, the fifty-move rule and insufficient material are draws). A game that reaches {{maxMoves}} moves each is stopped and scored on material. A win counts 1 point, a draw half a point.
chess/chess/still-your-move: Game {{game}}, move {{moveNo}}: it is still your move. Play a legal move with playMove; viewBoard shows the position again.
chess/chess/threats:
Loose pieces (attacked and undefended, or attacked by a cheaper piece; a static check, it does not see pins or what a move changes):
White: {{white}}.
Black: {{black}}.
chess/chess/tools/playMove: Play your move in the chess game, only when it is your move. Write it in standard algebraic notation (Nf3, exd5, O-O, e8=Q) or as from and to squares (g1f3, e7e8q). An illegal or unreadable move is refused and you may try again; the board does not change.
chess/chess/tools/resign: Resign the running game, only when it is your move. The opponent wins the game; the match goes on with the next game.
chess/chess/tools/viewBoard: Look at the chess board: the position (White at the bottom), whose move it is, the moves of the game so far, the material, and the game's number in the match.
chess/chess/your-move: Game {{game}}, move {{moveNo}}: {{colour}} to move, it is your move.
